content.user_title: Route WordPress Tasks to the Right Workflow
content.value_statement: WordPress repositories can be hard to classify before edits begin. This skill triages the project and routes work to the right WordPress workflow.
actual_capabilities: Classifies WordPress repositories by type using triage output.
Routes plugin, theme, block, REST API, WP-CLI, testing, performance, and security tasks.
Uses a decision tree to choose the most relevant domain workflow.
Applies guardrails for version constraints and existing project tooling.
Recommends lint, test, and build verification based on detected tooling.
limitations: Requires access to the repository root and the user intent.
Depends on a triage script that is not included in this package.
Routes to domain workflows but does not implement those workflows itself.
May ask a clarifying question when repository type is ambiguous.

use_cases.title: Classify a WordPress Plugin Repository
use_cases.description: Identify plugin signals, available tooling, and the correct plugin workflow before editing.

use_cases.title: Route Theme and Block Theme Work
use_cases.description: Separate classic theme tasks from block theme tasks before changing templates or theme settings.

use_cases.title: Plan Work in a Full Site Repository
use_cases.description: Find whether a request belongs to plugin, theme, REST API, testing, or operations work.

prompt_templates.title: Classify This Repository
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner triage before any WordPress edit.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the WordPress router on this repository. Tell me whether it is a plugin, theme, block theme, core checkout, or full site.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Select the right domain skill for a known task.
prompt_templates.prompt: Route this WordPress task to the correct workflow: I need to change a REST endpoint and verify permissions.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect Tooling and Tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Triage this WordPress codebase, identify available tooling, and recommend the lint, test, or build commands to run.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve Ambiguous Routing
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for a mixed repository.
prompt_templates.prompt: This repository contains plugins, themes, and wp-content. Route my performance task and state any assumptions or clarifying question.

output_examples.input: I need to add a settings page to this WordPress plugin.
output_examples.output: The skill classifies the request as plugin development and routes it to hooks, admin pages, and Settings API workflow guidance.

output_examples.input: This project has theme templates and theme settings. Where should I start?
output_examples.output: The skill checks whether the repository is a classic theme or block theme, then routes changes to the matching theme workflow.

output_examples.input: Help me debug a slow WordPress editor experience.
output_examples.output: The skill routes the task to performance guidance after checking project type, tooling, tests, and version constraints.

best_practices: Run triage before selecting a WordPress workflow.
Confirm WordPress core and PHP targets when detection is unclear.
Use the repository existing lint, test, and build commands.
anti_patterns: Do not assume every WordPress repository is a plugin.
Do not run unrelated tooling before reading triage output.
Do not bypass version constraints or release requirements.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It classifies a WordPress codebase and routes the task to the most relevant workflow.

faq.question: Does it edit WordPress code directly?
faq.answer: No. It helps choose the correct workflow before another skill or agent performs the change.

faq.question: Which repository types can it classify?
faq.answer: It covers plugins, must-use plugins, classic themes, block themes, full sites, WordPress core, and Gutenberg repositories.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, or Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it require WP-CLI?
faq.answer: Not always. Some routed workflows may require WP-CLI, depending on the repository and task.

faq.question: What should I provide before using it?
faq.answer: Provide the repository root, the user intent, version targets, and any release or platform constraints.
